title: Muscular characteristics in obstructive sleep apnea – a prospective controlled MRI analysis
summary:
The planned prospective controlled study investigates whether the muscles in the oral and pharyngeal regions differ between individuals with and without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), as well as with and without nocturnal teeth grinding/clenching or jaw muscle tension (sleep bruxism, SB). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), a specialized form of imaging, will be used for this purpose.

Obstructive sleep apnea is a widespread sleep disorder in which the upper airways repeatedly collapse during sleep, leading to reduced oxygen supply to the body. This can result in serious health problems such as high blood pressure, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic disorders. Obstructive sleep apnea is particularly common among older adults—up to 38% of adults are affected.

In our previous clinical prevalence study, we found that people with sleep apnea were about three times more likely to suffer from nocturnal teeth grinding/clenching or jaw muscle tension than those without sleep apnea. These patients also exhibited a higher muscle tone—that is, an increased baseline tension of the jaw muscles—across all sleep stages. Bruxism events frequently occurred simultaneously with brief awakenings or breathing pauses, suggesting a link between sleep bruxism and obstructive sleep apnea.

The aim of the planned clinical research project is therefore to investigate anatomical and functional characteristics, as well as differences in cortisol levels, in patients with OSA (OSA-positive group), both with and without sleep bruxism, and in patients without OSA (OSA-negative group), also both with and without sleep bruxism.

interventions.name:
Patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA-positive group):
- Diagnostic polysomnography with additional EMG electrodes 
- Examination of inclusion and exclusion criteria.
- Assignment to the OSA-positive group with AHI ≥ 5.
- Information and consent
- Clinical dental examination: examination o

Patients without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA-negative group):
- Diagnostic polysomnography with additional EMG electrodes
- Examination of inclusion and exclusion criteria.
- Assignment to the OSA-positive group with AHI < 5.
- Information and consent
- Clinical dental examination: examination

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- OSA (AHI > 5) and healthy control (AHI < 5)
- Signed informed consent
- Age 18–99 years
- Clinically and anamnestically confirmed sleep bruxism
- Clinically and anamnestically unconfirmed sleep bruxism
Exclusion criteria:
- Neuropathic pain
- Respiratory insufficiency
- Analgesic medication with potential impact on muscle or respiratory function
- Malignant diseases
- Severe psychiatric disorders
- History of extensive surgeries in the head, jaw, or facial region (e.g., major trauma, cleft lip and palate surgery)
- Cognitive impairments
- Other sleep disorders (e.g., REM sleep behavior disorder, insomnia, periodic limb movement disorder [PLMD])
- Use of psychotropic medication
- < 4 hours of sleep recorded during polysomnography or polygraphy
- History of surgical interventions for OSA treatment
- Lack of informed consent regarding incidental findings (see MRI consent form)
- Cardiac pacemakers
- Implantable defibrillators
- Left ventricular assist devices (LVADs)
- Cochlear implants
- Implanted insulin pumps (external pumps must be removed prior to imaging)
- Neurostimulators
- Penile prostheses
- Bladder pacemakers
- Ferromagnetic surgical clips, e.g., post-carotid endarterectomy or neurosurgical procedures
- Metallic foreign bodies in critical locations (e.g., eye, brain, intrathoracic or vascular regions)
- Vascular stents implanted less than 72 hours prior to imaging
- Joint prostheses or metallic implants for bone stabilization if implanted less than 6 weeks prior to imaging (Note: Titanium implants are generally MRI-compatible after 6 weeks)
- Recent myocardial infarction or vascular stents implanted less than 72 hours ago
- Large tattoos with metal-containing pigments
- Metallic transdermal or subdermal implants
- Piercings must be able to be removed for the examination
